issues.legal_issue: Promoting trade, commerce, and industry may be an object of general public utility even when the benefits are shared by a defined section of the public.
material_facts: The organization's principal objects were to promote, protect, and develop trade, commerce, and industry, with the stated aim extending beyond the interests of its members.
Its property income was legally required to be applied solely toward the organization's stated objects.
issues.conclusion: The organization's trade-promoting objects were charitable objects of general public utility, and the property income held for those objects qualified for exemption.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 4(3)(i) of the Indian Income-tax Act, 1922, the inclusive definition of charitable purpose covers advancement of an object of general public utility. The benefit need not extend to all mankind; it is sufficient to benefit a sufficiently identifiable section of the public rather than specified individuals. The Court relied on Commissioners of Inland Revenue v. Yorkshire Agricultural Society and The Institution of Civil Engineers v. Commissioners of Inland Revenue, and disapproved the contrary interpretation in Commissioner of Income-tax v. The Grain Merchants' Association of Bombay.

rule.if: income_tax_exemption_claim and property_legally_dedicated and trade_promotion_is_primary and trade_promotion_benefits_a_public_section

predicates.income_tax_exemption_claim: The taxpayer sought exemption from income tax for income derived from property.
predicates.property_legally_dedicated: The property income was legally required to be applied to the organization's stated purposes.
predicates.trade_promotion_is_primary: The organization's principal purpose was to promote, protect, or develop trade, commerce, or industry.
predicates.trade_promotion_benefits_a_public_sectio: The organization's trade-promoting activities were intended to benefit a sufficiently identifiable section of the public, not only specified individuals.

issues.definition: When a taxpayer claims exemption for legally dedicated property income and its primary trade-promoting purpose benefits a public section, the property income is exempt.

issues.legal_issue: A public-utility purpose is not too vague merely because the organization's objects do not specify the methods by which they are to be achieved.
material_facts: The organization's principal objects described the promotion, protection, assistance, and development of trade, commerce, and industry.
The memorandum did not prescribe the particular methods or steps for achieving those objects.
issues.conclusion: The organization's objects were not vague or indefinite merely because their methods of achievement were unspecified.
issues.legal_principle: For purposes of section 4(3)(i) of the Indian Income-tax Act, 1922, an object of general public utility such as promoting or protecting trade, commerce, and industry need not specify the modus or steps by which it will be achieved. The Court distinguished Runchordas Vandrawandas v. Parvati Bai, Commissioners of Inland Revenue v. National Anti-Vivisection Society, and Baddeley v. Commissioners of Inland Revenue.

predicates.income_tax_exemption_claim: The taxpayer sought exemption from income tax for income derived from property.
predicates.general_public_utility_object: The organization's stated object was directed to a public utility purpose.
predicates.achievement_methods_unspecified: The organization's governing documents did not prescribe the particular methods for achieving that purpose.

issues.definition: When an exemption claim concerns a public-utility object, leaving the methods of achievement unspecified does not make the object insufficiently definite.

issues.legal_issue: Incidental benefits to an organization's members do not prevent its public-utility purpose from being charitable.
material_facts: The organization's work could benefit people engaged in trade and commerce, including its members.
Its stated objects extended to the commercial interests of the country and were not confined to benefits for its members.
The organization's income and property could not be distributed to members as profit.
issues.conclusion: The possibility that members might benefit incidentally did not prevent the organization from being established for charitable purposes.
issues.legal_principle: Section 4(3)(i) of the Indian Income-tax Act, 1922, does not exclude a public-utility purpose merely because members also benefit in carrying it out; the question is whether personal benefit is so substantial that it cannot be disregarded. The Court relied on Commissioners of Inland Revenue v. Yorkshire Agricultural Society and The Institution of Civil Engineers v. Commissioners of Inland Revenue.

predicates.income_tax_exemption_claim: The taxpayer sought exemption from income tax for income derived from property.
predicates.public_benefit_is_primary: The organization's main purpose was directed to benefiting the public or a section of the public, rather than serving its members alone.
predicates.member_benefits_are_incidental: Any benefits members received arose incidentally from the organization's pursuit of its public purpose.

issues.definition: When the primary purpose benefits the public and member benefits are incidental, those member benefits do not defeat charitable status.

issues.legal_issue: Ancillary advocacy concerning legislation does not defeat charitable status when the organization's primary purpose is the advancement of a public-utility object.
material_facts: The organization's primary objects were to promote and protect trade, commerce, and industry and their general commercial interests.
One stated object allowed the organization to urge or oppose legislative and other measures affecting trade, commerce, or manufacture.
The legislative advocacy was directed toward achieving the primary objects and was not itself the organization's primary purpose.
issues.conclusion: The organization's ancillary advocacy concerning legislation did not prevent its primary public-utility purpose from being charitable.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 4(3)(i) of the Indian Income-tax Act, 1922, an organization remains charitable where its primary purpose advances an object of general public utility, even if it contemplates incidental political activity to achieve that purpose. The Court relied on In re The Trustees of the Tribune and All India Spinners' Association v. Commissioner of Income-tax, and distinguished Laxman Balwant Bhopatkar v. Charity Commissioner, Bombay, where the primary purpose was political.

predicates.income_tax_exemption_claim: The taxpayer sought exemption from income tax for income derived from property.
predicates.public_utility_purpose_is_primary: The organization's principal purpose was to advance an object of general public utility.
predicates.legislative_advocacy_is_ancillary: The organization contemplated urging or opposing legislation only as an incidental means of achieving its principal public-utility purpose.

issues.definition: When an organization's primary purpose advances public utility and its legislative advocacy is ancillary to that purpose, the advocacy does not defeat charitable status.
